title: 2011 AMC 8 Problem 13
statement: Two congruent squares, \(ABCD\) and \(PQRS,\) have side length \(15.\) They overlap to form the \(15\) by \(25\) rectangle \(AQRD\) shown. What percent of the area of rectangle \(AQRD\) is shaded?

solutions.text:
We get that \[\begin{align*} SC &= DC + SR - DR \\ &= 15 + 15 - 25 \\ &= 5. \end{align*}\]

This means that the area of \(PBSC\) is \(5 \cdot 15 = 75.\) The area of \(AQRD\) is \(25 \cdot 15 = 375.\)

\(\dfrac{75}{375} = \dfrac{1}{5},\) which is \(20 \%.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Compare the shaded rectangle area with the area of the \(15\) by \(25\) rectangle.
The overlap is a rectangle whose width is the sum of two side lengths minus \(25\).
